attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: Faithful to the universal 'every AI startup is unprofitable' and its stated consequence. The conditional about rate spikes is a separate clause and is rightly left out.

contract.note: 'Every' is universal, so one credible counterexample contradicts it. Ordinary-sense profitability and a window of about a year before the post are fair readings. The speaker named no accounting basis.

evidence.note: Nov 2025 news restatement of Gamma's announcement: profitable for over two years. This is a company disclosure, which the contract accepts. It falls inside the period.
July 2025 SiliconANGLE, citing Reuters: bootstrapped Surge AI is said to be profitable on $1B+ revenue. Sourcing is anonymous but reputable. A second counterexample.
Aug 2026 contributed article with the Gamma CEO saying it is profitable. It was published after the post and describes a later time, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: The claim is universal. Gamma's own disclosure, restated in the press, and Reuters-sourced reporting on Surge AI both describe AI startups that were profitable during 2025, before the March 2026 post. Neither figure is audited, but the contract accepts company-reported or reputable press profitability. One counterexample is enough to contradict 'every'.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Two-part observation: heavy reliance on debt, and debt getting harder to raise. 'Before the war' is a fair reading of 'already' in context. Dropping the clause on chip and construction costs is minor.

contract.note: 'Endless' is read fairly as heavy, ongoing borrowing. 'Difficult to raise' is undefined, and the contract's rule (mixed if the strain is limited to some borrowers while the broad market absorbed deals) is a reasonable, ordinary reading. The result turns on that interpretation.

evidence.note: Reuters, Nov 2025: data centers increasingly financed with debt, with record AI investment-grade issuance. Supports Part A.
Reuters, Dec 2025: Blue Owl talks on Oracle's Michigan project stalled. Weak support for Part B, since these were mainly equity talks and Oracle said it had other bidders.
Bloomberg, Feb 2026: Oracle's $25B bond drew record orders, and the market comfortably absorbed 2025's AI issuance. Cuts against any broad tightening.
Same Bloomberg piece: for weeks before Feb 2026, Oracle's debt traded like junk. Borrowing got costlier for a key AI data center borrower.
May 2026 report that banks spent six months or more placing the $38B Oracle-linked loan. It was published after the post and the pre-war part of the timing is only implied, so it is context.

reviews.rationale: Part A holds: AI data center buildout leaned heavily on debt in late 2025. Part B holds only partly. There was strain for Oracle-linked borrowers (junk-like pricing, a stalled Blue Owl deal), but Oracle's Feb 2026 bond drew record demand and the market broadly absorbed AI issuance. Under the contract's own rule, the result is mixed.
